equity_bridge.note: FY2026 10-K: $684M net receivable at 2026-05-31 from the Supreme Court tariff ruling, carried at 75% for the tax already provided in FY2026 but likely paid in FY2027 cash. Collected in FY2027 outside the modelled flows (wc_capture tracks revenue change only). Worth ~$0.35/share.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case long-run revenue growth (terminal), the nearest historical anchor being the equity 5yr CAGR of 3.1%; FY2021->FY2026 windows (FY2021 44,538 / FY2023 51,217 -> FY2026 46,398)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (+3.1% 5yr) diverges by far more than 30% from EPS (-10.4%) and owner-FCF (-25.8%) CAGRs: book value is flattered by the near-halt in buybacks since FY2025, while earnings and cash flow describe the FY2024-26 trough. None of the trailing CAGRs is a forward growth anchor; the base path is built from FY2027 guidance and a mid-cycle margin recovery instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - interest income (FY2021 interest income approximated at ~$50M; FY2023 297; FY2026 278). Owner-FCF CAGRs are ~7-9pp/yr worse than reported-FCF CAGRs because SBC rose from 0.8% of revenue pre-2020 to 1.5% while cash flow fell, and interest income on the cash pile grew from ~$35M to ~$300-430M/yr. FY2026 owner FCF of $1.19B (2.6% of revenue) is also depressed by a ~$1.5B working-capital drag (OCF 2,868 vs NI+D&A+SBC 4,570), part of which is the uncollected tariff receivable.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2027 lands on guidance (revenue -8%, adjusted EPS ~$1.25 before ~$0.15 of Pace restructuring) as Greater China keeps shrinking, classics (Dunk, AF1) stay throttled and Converse declines. From FY2028 the wholesale reset (Foot Locker, Dick's, JD, Amazon) and the running-category relaunch hold North America and EMEA, China stops falling, and revenue grows mid-single digits for FY2029-31 before fading to 2.5%. Pace delivers most of its ~$2.5B savings but roughly half is reinvested in product and demand creation, and tariffs (~3% of revenue gross) are only partly offset by sourcing shifts out of China and price, so the pre-SBC EBITDA margin recovers to 14.5% -- a mid-cycle level below both FY2016-19 and the FY2021-22 peak. Capex steps up to ~2% of revenue for the supply-chain modernisation. Share count flat; buybacks resume only as cash allows.
scenario_narratives.bull: The turnaround proves out faster: FY2027 revenue falls only 6% as the Amazon/wholesale restocking and new running franchises (Pegasus, Vomero, Structure) outrun the classics decline; FY2028 returns to +4% and compounds at 5-6% through FY2031 as Nike reclaims running share from Hoka/On and Greater China recovers from its -26% trough. Pace savings are largely retained, tariff mitigation completes by FY2028 (China sourcing to high-single digits), and gross margin returns to the mid-40s, lifting the pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 16.5% -- the FY2016-19 range plus structural cost-out, still below the FY2021-22 peak. Terminal growth 3%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The air pocket is deeper and the share loss is permanent: FY2027 revenue falls 10% and FY2028 another 4% as China keeps declining, lifestyle demand shifts to Adidas/New Balance/On/Hoka, Converse continues to shrink and the wholesale reset brings back retailer margin pressure without the volume. Revenue then only tracks ~2% nominal growth. Tariffs remain a ~3% permanent cost, Pace savings are competed away in price and marketing, and the pre-SBC EBITDA margin settles at 11% -- roughly the FY2025-26 trough level with the one-offs stripped. This is a shrunken but still solidly profitable brand; the model does not price distress (net cash, investment-grade notes).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value NIKE as a mid-cycle recovery, not at the FY2026-27 trough and not at the FY2021-22 peak. The flows are owner FCF (SBC expensed, share count flat, interest income stripped with the gross cash credited once), built from components so that the margin path -- the single biggest judgment -- is explicit: FY2027 anchored to guidance including the restructuring cash, recovering over seven years to a 14.5% pre-SBC EBITDA margin. Discounted at a single 9% USD WACC with the turnaround, China and tariff risk carried in the scenario flows and a 25/50/25 weighting. Terminal value is Gordon at 2.5% (the 18x FCF cap is not binding at 9%).
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin path: every 1pp of terminal pre-SBC EBITDA margin is worth roughly $2.5-3/share; the base 14.5% assumes tariffs and the wholesale mix are only partly structural
FY2028 inflection: if revenue falls again in FY2028 (bear) rather than stabilising, the base path's mid-single-digit FY2029-31 recovery has no base to compound from
Greater China: ~13% of revenue falling 26% with local competitors (Anta, Li-Ning) gaining; the base assumes it stops falling, not that it recovers
Tariff policy volatility in both directions: the ~$1.5B annual gross cost is modelled as partly permanent; a refund-style reversal or a further escalation each move value by several dollars a share
Cash tax: 24-26% is above the 15-19% historical ETR; if earnings mix normalises the ETR could fall back, which is upside not in the base
Balance-sheet vintage: anchors are the 2026-05-31 10-K; the Q1 FY2027 10-Q (Aug-2026) was not yet filed at build time

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close on the Q1 FY2027 print day); 52-week range 35.02-74.78
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 320187): FY2026 10-K filed 2026-07-15 and FY2026 10-Qs, via research/NKE/Reports/NKE_Metrics.csv and direct tag lookups for debt split, short-term investments, lease liabilities, working-capital balances, interest paid and the tariff receivable
data_sources.qualitative: research/NKE/Reports/NKE_Analysis.json (2026-10-02): Q1 FY2027 results and FY2027 guidance (2026-10-01), 'Pace' restructuring plan, tariff and China commentary

inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement, us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation $715M (XBRL, filed 2026-07-15). Nike publishes no combined SBC-plus-withholding figure; PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation has not been tagged since FY2019 (then $17-55M/yr, <0.15% of revenue), so no withholding add-on is made.
inputs.share_count_basis: FY2026 diluted weighted-average shares, us-gaap:WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding 1,481.0M (basic 1,479.8M). Cover-page count is not XBRL-tagged post-2015; FY2026 buybacks were only $146M so the diluted average is within ~0.3% of the period-end count. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would double-charge it.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-01T20:00:02Z regular close (the Q1 FY2027 print day; the stock fell on the print and is at the bottom of its 52-week range, so the anchor is live but volatile)
inputs.net_debt_note: Debt = us-gaap:LongTermDebt $7,942M at 2026-05-31 (non-current 5,942 + current 2,000). The DB/CSV total_debt of 9,942 double-counts the current portion (same XBRL-pipeline bug as FCX and KEYS) and is NOT used. Cash = cash and equivalents 7,563 + short-term investments (DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleExcludingAccruedInterestCurrent) 1,464 = 9,027. Net cash 1,085. Interest income (278) is stripped from the FCF base because the gross cash pile is credited here; reported FCF is also after $323M of interest paid, which the unlevered component build does not carry, so the unlevered FY0 equivalent of last_fcf is ~1.44B.
inputs.lease_treatment: ASC 842 operating leases (liability $3,091M at 2026-05-31; cash payments $668M in FY2026) are an operating cost already inside SG&A, EBITDA and operating cash flow. Treatment (B): lease cost stays in the EBITDA margin path, lease liabilities are EXCLUDED from net debt, and no separate lease_cost_pct_path is charged. Charged exactly once.
inputs.nci_treatment: None: NIKE has no material non-controlling interests.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD WACC. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST, Oct 2026), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.1 -> cost of equity ~9.7%; after-tax cost of debt ~3.5% on $7.9B of fixed-rate notes; ~13% debt weight at the current ~$52B market cap -> ~8.9%, rounded to 9.0%. The same 9.0% is used in all three scenarios: turnaround, China and tariff risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company, consumer/cyclical'; adaptations file read for leases, working-capital sign and charge-risk-once). Fresh build, first valuation of this ticker. NIKE is in an earnings trough: FY2026 revenue $46.4B flat on FY2025, pre-SBC EBITDA margin ~11.7% (FY2021-22 peak ~18%, FY2016-19 ~15-16.5%), and FY2027 guidance is a high-single-digit revenue decline with adjusted EPS $1.15-1.35 ex ~$0.15 of 'Pace' restructuring. The base case neither extrapolates the trough nor the peak: FY2027 is built to the guidance (incl. restructuring cash), and the pre-SBC EBITDA margin recovers to 14.5% by FY2034 -- below the pre-pandemic 15-16% because tariffs (~$1.5B gross, ~3% of revenue, only partly mitigated), the deliberate mix shift back to wholesale and lost running share are treated as partly structural, with the ~$2.5B Pace savings partly reinvested. Buybacks: $146M in FY2026 versus $3-5.5B/yr in FY2022-25; the flat count is a modelling convention the company is currently funding only via SBC-sized repurchases, which is fine because SBC is expensed. Working capital: receivables 5,931 + inventory 7,501 - payables 3,600 = ~$9.8B (21% of revenue), so wc_capture is NEGATIVE (-15%): growth consumes cash and the FY2027 revenue decline releases it. Cash tax: FY2026 cash taxes 1,270 on pretax 3,900 (33%) exceeded the 20% GAAP provision because of TCJA transition-tax instalments (final instalment FY2026); FY2027 guided ETR is mid-20s, so the cash rate is set at 26% easing to 24% rather than the 15-19% historical ETR. FY2026 net income includes a one-off tariff-refund gain (Supreme Court ruling; ~$986M disclosed, $684M net receivable at 2026-05-31); it is excluded from the forward margin paths and the receivable is carried in equity_bridge after tax. Capex rises from 1.5% of revenue to ~2.0% for Pace supply-chain modernisation and the India campus. The Q1 FY2027 10-Q (quarter ended 2026-08-31) was not yet on EDGAR at build time; the balance sheet is the FY2026 10-K, four months old.

base.ebitda_margin_note: Pre-SBC EBITDA = GAAP EBIT + D&A + SBC. FY2026 actual ~11.7% but ~9.5% ex the one-off tariff-refund gain. FY2027 8.6% reproduces the guidance midpoint ($1.25 adj EPS, mid-20s tax) after ~$290M pre-tax Pace restructuring cash; FY2028 still carries restructuring and early savings; recovery to 14.5% by FY2034 is ~1pp below FY2016-19 and ~3.5pp below the FY2021-22 peak.
base.growth_note: FY2027 -8% = 'high-single-digit decline' guidance (Q1 was -4%, so the back half is guided worse: China -26%, Dunk/classics throttled, Converse). FY2028 +1% as the wholesale reset and running launches offset a still-shrinking China; mid-single-digit FY2029-31 as share stabilises; fades to 2.5% terminal. Revenue regains the FY2023-24 ~$51B level only in FY2033.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Shifted from the house 15/50/35 to 25/50/25. Bear up to 25%: the thesis rests on an unproven turnaround that is now in its second restructuring plan after two years, FY2027 guidance says the bottom is not yet visible, and China (~13% of revenue) is still falling 26%. Bull down to 25%: it needs China stabilisation, running share recovery AND margin repair from tariffs and Pace to all land together. Base 50%: the balance sheet (net cash, no refinancing risk) and brand make a shrunken-but-profitable outcome the modal case, not a solvency case.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
